body.x: AllCOM (CEO Seunghyuk Jang) participates in ‘MWC (Mobile World Congress) 2026,’ held in Barcelona, Spain, from March 2 to 5 (local time), showcasing a smart tumbler capable of precise temperature control.

Founded in 2024, AllCOM derives its name from “All Comfort.” Headquartered in the Venture Business Incubation Center of Kumoh National Institute of Technology in Gumi, Gyeongbuk, the company was founded on the vision of ‘providing comfortable products to the market.’ Its very first item, this smart temperature-control tumbler, earned the CES 2026 Innovation Award 15 months after the company’s founding—even before its official launch—recognizing its technical prowess on the global stage. It is considered unusual for a nurtured company from the Gyeongbuk Gumi Gangso Special R&D Zone to sweep international innovation awards in such a short period.

The core of the smart tumbler unveiled at MWC 2026 is its ‘temperature modulation’ function. According to CEO Jang, existing tumblers and thermos products focus only on heating and maintaining temperature, with virtually no products allowing users to adjust the temperature precisely to their desired level. AllCOM’s product can adjust the temperature from 1°C to 85°C, and a sterilization effect can be expected at temperatures above 72°C.

The capacity is 20 ounces (591ml), approximately three times the 200ml capacity of existing overseas competitors. The water container part is detachable from the main body, making it dishwasher safe, and its battery-powered design allows for free outdoor use without a power source. It also features remote temperature setting via smartphone and tablet apps, with the final launch version planned to support home networking integration.

body.cap: Three types of AllCOM brand smart tumblers are on display. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The design philosophy of this product is the ‘integration of fixed and portable use.’ In the existing childcare market, parents had to purchase a domestic formula warmer (fixed) and an outdoor thermos (portable) separately, with combined costs reaching 270,000 to 300,000 KRW. AllCOM’s smart tumbler covers all functions of a fixed warmer while remaining portable, replacing two products with one.

The estimated launch price is between 150,000 and 190,000 KRW, roughly half the cost of purchasing separate units. “Instead of buying two, our single product is sufficient. While typical warmers are difficult to dispose of after the childcare period, our product can continue to be used for exercise or outdoor activities,” Jang emphasized. He also noted that AllCOM is the only company in Korea that offers a service in which breast milk can be collected via a pump, stored in a tumbler at a controlled temperature, and carried around.

Jang also expressed confidence in scalability beyond the childcare market. “In midsummer, people often throw away water left in cars because it gets too hot, but with our product, you can drink it at the desired temperature immediately because it operates on a battery. In winter, you don’t need to melt frozen water; just set the heating temperature,” he said. He revealed a roadmap to expand temperature control technology from tumblers to various household goods, stating, “Our future goal is to become a global ‘Therm Solution’ company.”

AllCOM matched with buyers from the U.S., UK, and Japan through its participation in CES 2026 this January and is currently in detailed negotiations. Its participation in MWC 2026 is also a move to meet European buyers directly.

A startup in its 15th month is carrying the momentum of a CES Innovation Award to another global stage like MWC. Attention is now focused on whether this move will lead to a successful entry into the European market.

MWC (Mobile World Congress) 2026, hosted by the GSMA (Global System for Mobile Communications Association), is held at the Fira Gran Via exhibition center in Barcelona, Spain, under the theme ‘The IQ Era’. This year’s event is the largest ever, with approximately 2,900 companies from 205 countries and more than 100,000 visitors participating. Major exhibition fields encompass the entire ICT industry, including AI infrastructure, 5G Advanced, and 6G preliminary technology, mobility, and fintech. Additionally, more than 200 conference sessions involving global leaders run in parallel during the exhibition period.
